title: Not Really Up for Karaoke
scene: After lunch on Sunday, a friend suggests karaoke. You're tired and would rather talk somewhere quiet, so you suggest coffee without dismissing his idea. It turns out he wanted a slower afternoon too.
sceneJa: 日曜の昼食後。友人にカラオケへ誘われるが、今日は静かに過ごしたい。相手の気分を損なわないようコーヒーを提案すると、実は友人も同じ気持ちだった。

chunks.ja: ケンがカラオケに行こうと提案したけれど

chunks.en: but I was still tired from the morning.
chunks.ja: 僕は午前中の疲れがまだ残っていた

chunks.en: I didn't want to ruin his plans,
chunks.ja: 彼の予定に水を差したくはなかった

chunks.en: but I wasn't really up for singing.
chunks.ja: でも、歌う気分にはあまりなれなかった
そこで、こう聞いてみた

chunks.en: "Would you be open to getting coffee instead?"
chunks.ja: 「代わりにコーヒーでも飲みに行くのはどう？」
彼も望んでいたのだった
僕らは小さなカフェを見つけて

chunks.en: without either of us having to sing a single note.
chunks.ja: どちらも一音たりとも歌わずに済んだ

questions.question: Which chunking keeps the conversational expression together?
options: I wasn't really / up for singing / but I
I wasn't really up for singing / but I wanted to be polite
I wasn't / really up / for singing but
questions.explanation: ‘Be up for (doing) something’ means to feel willing or in the mood to do it. ‘I wasn't really up for singing’ is a natural unit.

questions.question: What does ‘Would you be open to getting coffee instead?’ mean here?
options: Would you consider coffee as an alternative?
Do you want to open a coffee shop?
Have you already bought the coffee?
questions.explanation: ‘Would you be open to ...?’ gently asks whether someone would consider an option. ‘To’ is a preposition here, so it is followed by ‘getting’.

questions.question: Why does the narrator suggest coffee rather than simply refuse karaoke?
options: He wants to spend time with Ken while choosing a quieter activity.
He secretly wants Ken to go to karaoke alone.
He wants to cancel their friendship plans entirely.
questions.explanation: The speaker doesn't feel like singing but still wants to spend time together. The alternative protects the relationship while expressing a preference.

speak: Imagine a friend suggests a noisy activity but you'd prefer something quieter. Round 1: Read ‘I wasn't really up for singing’ and ‘Would you be open to getting coffee instead?’ slowly, keeping each phrase together. Round 2: Say ‘Would you be open to ...?’ with a warm, rising tone; answer ‘Actually, that works for me’ with relaxed agreement. Round 3: Read the six-sentence story aloud, changing your tone from hesitant to relieved. Speak for 30 seconds: Politely decline one activity, offer an alternative, and respond to your friend's choice. Final Read: Read the entire story again without the Japanese translation.
review: Lesson 94: ‘It turns out ...’ (実は〜だったと分かった) becomes ‘It turned out he'd been hoping for a quieter afternoon too’ (話してみると、彼も静かな午後を望んでいた) in a past-tense conversation story. Lesson 93: ‘for a moment’ (少しの間) reappears in ‘He thought for a moment’ (彼は少し考えた). New: ‘not really up for ...’ (〜する気分ではない), ‘Would you be open to ...?’ (〜を検討してくれる？), ‘That works for me’ (それで大丈夫). Naturalness checked against Cambridge Dictionary's ‘up for (doing) something’ definition and usage.
